title: SimVLA: Attributing Gains in VLA Models Through Controlled Ablation
abstract: arXiv:2602.18224v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models often bundle architectural changes with different pretraining data, backbone scales, and optimization recipes, obscuring what actually drives progress. We introduce SimVLA, a deliberately minimal VLA, a standard vision-language backbone with a lightweight continuous-action head, as a controlled testbed for this attribution problem; our contribution is methodological and empirical (a controlled attribution study and a minimal-baseline calibration), not a new technique. Across LIBERO, CALVIN, WidowX, and Google Robot, one-knob-at-a-time ablations show that training dynamics are the largest measured driver, producing performance swings of $\Delta$$\approx$54--94\%, while task configuration and architecture have smaller effects under matched settings. translated_title: SimVLA：通过受控消融实验归因VLA模型的性能提升
translated_abstract: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型通常将架构变更与不同的预训练数据、骨干网络规模和优化方案捆绑在一起，这使得究竟是什么因素真正推动了进步变得模糊不清。我们提出了SimVLA——一个刻意极简的VLA模型，即一个标准的视觉-语言骨干网络加上一个轻量级的连续动作头——作为解决这一归因问题的受控实验平台；我们的贡献是方法论和实证层面的（一项受控归因研究和一个最小基线校准），而非一种新技术。在LIBERO、CALVIN、WidowX和Google Robot四个基准上，一次只改变一个变量的消融实验表明，训练动态是测量出的最大驱动因素，可产生约54%–94%的性能波动，而在匹配设置下，任务配置和架构的影响较小。尽管SimVLA使用了小型骨干网络，且在针对基准的训练之前没有进行额外的大规模机器人数据VLA预训练，其仍达到了98.6%的……
tldr: 该论文提出刻意极简的VLA基线模型SimVLA作为受控实验平台，通过单变量消融实验发现训练动态（而非架构或任务配置）才是VLA模型性能提升的最大驱动因素，可带来约54%–94%的性能波动。
en_tdlr: SimVLA, a deliberately minimal VLA baseline, serves as a controlled testbed whose one-knob-at-a-time ablations reveal that training dynamics—rather than architecture or task configuration—are the largest driver of performance gains in VLA models, producing swings of about 54–94%.
